name: Declarative Clause

dimensions.form: Clause headed by a VP, with an optional Subject and no interrogative, exclamative, or imperative clause-type marking
dimensions.meaning: Presents propositional content without encoding an open or closed question, remarkable degree, or imperative marking as clause type
dimensions.function: Characteristically makes a statement, but also supports directives, promises, questions, and other forces
dimensions.distribution: The default clause type; occurs as a main clause and as a subordinate content clause

1.definition: The default headed clause type, characteristically used to make a statement
1.details: Declarative is a category of syntactic form, not a statement-force category. Basic declaratives normally have Subject–Predicator order, but their actual force depends on construction and context: Passengers are requested to remain seated is a directive, and a declarative question adds question intonation to declarative syntax. Declaratives occur both as main clauses and as subordinate content clauses (CGEL pp. 853–55, 951–55).

examples.note: Main declarative in its characteristic statement use
Declarative clause used as a directive; force does not determine clause type

examples.form: She says [that Kim finished the report].

constraints.description: The construction is a Clause headed by VP, with an optional Subject; declarative is the default type and lacks the specialized type-marking properties of closed interrogatives, open interrogatives, exclamatives, and imperatives.
Statement is the characteristic use, not a necessary condition: declarative syntax is compatible with indirect questions and directives and with performative forces such as promising.

projection.target: Basic declarative clause structure predicts broad main- and subordinate-clause distribution and leaves illocutionary force comparatively open, while making statement force the unmarked interpretation in an independent assertion context
projection.evidence: CGEL contrasts the declarative's default Subject–Predicator organization and broad content-clause distribution with the specialized marking and distribution of the other four major clause types

grounds.note: Default declarative form projects broad main/subordinate distribution without fixing illocutionary force
The form/distribution profile recurs independently of characteristic statement use

diagnostics: absence of interrogative, exclamative, or imperative type marking

grounds.note: Declarative as the default major clause type, distinct from statement force, in main and subordinate clauses

curious.title: The plain statement-shaped sentence
curious.summary: A declarative sentence is the default sentence shape, and it is built for making statements but can do other jobs too.
curious.body:
Kim finished the report is the plainest kind of sentence. It has no question word, no exclamation form and no command form. This dictionary calls that shape declarative. It is the default type, and it turns up both as a sentence on its own and inside another sentence, as in She says that Kim finished the report.

Making a statement is the characteristic use of this shape, but the shape doesn't fix the job. Passengers are requested to remain seated has the same shape and works as a directive. Declarative names a form, not a purpose. This dictionary treats the analysis as provisional.

examples.text: She says [that Kim finished the report].

curious.try: Look at a sign or announcement that sounds like a statement. Is it telling you something, or asking you to do something?

teacher.summary: Helps separate declarative as a clause form from statement as a use, since declarative clauses can also direct, promise and ask.
teacher.explain: A declarative clause is the default headed clause type: a Clause headed by a VP, with an optional Subject, and no interrogative, exclamative or imperative marking. Basic declaratives normally have Subject-Predicator order. Declarative is a category of syntactic form, not statement force. Statement is the characteristic use, but force depends on construction and context: Passengers are requested to remain seated is a directive, and a declarative question adds question intonation to declarative syntax. Declaratives occur as main clauses and as subordinate content clauses. The analysis is provisional.
teacher.terms: Traditional grammars call this the declarative sentence and tie it to making statements. This dictionary separates clause type (declarative) from force (statement, directive and so on).

examples.text: She says [that Kim finished the report].

contrasts.note: Declarative form, used to make a statement.

contrasts.text: Passengers are requested to remain seated.
contrasts.note: Same form, used as a directive.

watch_for: A learner might assume that a declarative clause must make a statement, when its force depends on construction and context.
A learner might treat a clause inside another sentence, as in She says that Kim finished the report, as not declarative, when declaratives also occur as subordinate content clauses.
teacher.activity: Students collect short declarative sentences from notices and announcements around the school. They sort each by what it does (states, directs, promises, asks) and discuss how they can tell.
